question: Is it permissible to buy a dog with money?
asked: She came across a fatwa saying that even if she gets a dog, she cannot purchase it with money, because of a hadith forbidding the purchase of a dog. So how can she get the dog?
answer:
Apparently she's been reading the fatwas, and understandably she came across one that said she cannot purchase the dog; she must somehow acquire it or train it. And you have heard correctly: there is such a fatwa. In fact, this is based on the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, which is muttafaqun 'alayh, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade the price of a dog. What does this mean? It means that he considered it to be something that should not happen: you should not give money for a dog. This is the interpretation of the majority, that you should not purchase a dog with money.

And this is the standard position of a number of schools. This is the position of the Shafi'is and the Hanbalis, the majority position within the school; there are dissenting voices. And by the way, every time I give you a school, realize that you will always find within that school one or two or maybe more scholars who are disagreeing. I'm giving you the default, the main position.

So the Shafi'is and the Hanbalis, by and large, took this literally, and they said even if you need one of these dogs that are allowed, you need to either acquire it from a previous owner who no longer needs it, and he cannot sell it to you, or you need to get an untrained dog as a puppy and train it yourself, or have somebody come and train it, because you're allowed to pay the trainer. But according to these two schools, you cannot pay the price of the dog itself. And again, they based it on this hadith, that he forbade the price of the dog.

Now, the other two schools: the Hanafi school said that the dog is basically an animal, a beneficial animal in other circumstances, and like all other animals it can be bought and sold. Just because you cannot own a dog doesn't mean you cannot buy and sell it for a legitimate reason. And the Malikis as well said that any dog that can be acquired legally can be sold legally: a seeing dog, a protector dog, any dog that is now trained to do something that the Shariah allows. So whatever the Shariah allows, it should be allowed to buy and sell it. That's the Maliki ruling here.

And this does seem to be the stronger ruling, especially in light of the hadith in Sunan al-Nasa'i as well. There's an authentic hadith that our Prophet ﷺ forbade the purchase of a dog except for a hunting dog. So the exception is in the hadith itself: a hunting dog may be purchased and sold, no problem.

And therefore, to conclude this question, **you may purchase a dog for any legitimate reason**, not just those two or three mentioned in the hadith: any reason that makes sense, that is going to make your life easier for you, a seeing dog, anything of this nature, or a protection dog. Anything that will help you in your life and make it easier: it is permissible to acquire such a dog, and it is permissible to purchase such a dog with money as well. The only thing that we said you have to be careful about is the issue of the najasah of the saliva of the dog. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
